Synopsis:
An aggravated wolf in a druid grove. He has learned obedience from Rath but is still a wild thing at heart. There are newcomers to his home and his instincts tell him to chase them away, to harm them, but he's not allowed to. He's like a coiled spring, ready to strike.

Cluster Contexts:
- DEN_DruidServant_003.json: An elderly druid who would like nothing more than for the player to leave. Depending on what the player has done, he will be civil about it, but still incistent. If the child has died, he is openly hostile.
- DEN_AttackOnDen_Pet002.json: After victory following a huge goblin attack on his home, a wolf feels satisfied with a job well done, but warns you not to ruin the peace..
- DEN_DruidServant_002.json: A very condescending and somewhat objectionable druid servant. He believes the tiefling refugees hiding in the grove have brought chaos and would gladly be rid of them, even if turning them away would doom them.

- DEN_DruidAttack_AD_Refugee004.json: Toron, a tiefling, reacts to the druids attacking him and the other refugees sheltering in the grove.

retrieved_synopses: An elderly druid who would like nothing more than for the player to leave. Depending on what the player has done, he will be civil about it, but still incistent. If the child has died, he is openly hostile.
After victory following a huge goblin attack on his home, a wolf feels satisfied with a job well done, but warns you not to ruin the peace..

A very condescending and somewhat objectionable druid servant. He believes the tiefling refugees hiding in the grove have brought chaos and would gladly be rid of them, even if turning them away would doom them.
Halsin, arch-druid of the Emerald Grove, is  following the player inside the Goblin Camp in his bear form, trying to find and kill the goblin leadership. The player can tell him to hold his position.
Toron, a tiefling, reacts to the druids attacking him and the other refugees sheltering in the grove.
context: The scene takes place in a druid grove where an agitated wolf (Silver) lives; he’s been taught obedience by Rath but remains a wild, on-edge animal ready to strike. Newcomers — possibly the player and other refugees — have entered his territory and his instincts push him to chase or harm them, though Rath’s training and the druids’ rules hold him back. Off-screen, the grove is tense: some druid servants want outsiders gone (and can be openly hostile), the group has recently faced attacks (or defended against them), and there’s conflict over refugees sheltered here. The player’s offer to “give you my smell” is a pacifying gesture; the wolf’s words warn that any wrong move could still set him off.
